newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann Q1 growth meets expectations.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann Q1 growth meets expectations.

text.p: Germany's Mannesmann AG said on Monday its telecommunications unit sparked first-quarter sales to rise 14 percent to 8.1 billion marks ($4.8 billion).
The telecoms unit, which includes Germany's largest mobile phone network, saw sales rise 69 percent to 1.4 billion marks.

The company also said profit from ordinary activities rose and forecast an "improved earnings structure and a higher group result" for the whole of 1997 -- even though heavy investments in its fixed line telephone network would keep telecommunications profit flat.

The first quarter results were in line with analysts' expectations. "These numbers gave a confirmation of what the company said in April. It was no surprise," said Hermann Reith at BHF Bank in Frankfurt.
At 1230 GMT, Mannesmann shares traded at 726 marks, up two marks, rising with the blue-chip DAX index, which was up one percent at 3,641.27.
First-quarter orders rose 14 percent, to 10.2 billion marks, the Duesseldorf-based company said.
Within telecoms operations, Mannesmann Arcor, a venture formed last summer with the German railroad phone network DBKom and AT&T Corp., had 228 million marks in sales.

Mannesmann Mobilfunk -- which operates the D2 mobile network -- saw sales in the quarter rise 42 percent to 1.9 billion marks. The number of D2 customers rose by 200,000 in the first quarter, to about 2.5 million.
The company was investing heavily to modernise the railway phone network into a backbone Arcor can use to become the second phone company after Deutsche Telekom AG.
"Despite further increases in earnings at Mannesmann D2, telecommunications will remain flat due to start-up losses of new activities," the company said in a letter to shareholders.
About 1.8 billion marks in assets and goodwill resulting from the consolidation of Arcor pushed total investment in the quarter up 335 percent to 2.382 billion marks.
Reith said he expected Arcor and Cegetel, a venture involving the French railway's phone unit, to require further investments next year, but at lower levels.
"There should be further growth in telecom profit with Mobilfunk results increasing and losses in Arcor and Cegetel going down," he told Reuters.
The first quarter results were also helped by a turn around in the tubes and trading unit, which returned to profitability.

That unit, which entered into a joint venture with French steel tube maker Vallourec SA, saw first-quarter sales of 1.7 billion marks, up seven percent, and orders of 2.2 billion marks, up 27 percent.
The company's engineering unit reported a first-quarter loss due to seasonal factors, while its automotive technology business showed increased profit.
Engineering sales were up 11 percent to 2.8 billion marks, but orders were unchanged at 4.28 billion marks.
